assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and stochastic thermodynamics extended thermodynamic reasoning to small, driven, far-from-equilibrium systems, giving exact relations (Jarzynski equality, Crooks relation, steady-state and detailed fluctuation theorems) and a trajectory-level definition of heat, work and entropy production. This is a conceptual advance in statistical physics that reorganised how stochastic dynamics is treated, and it is central to my own field of stochastic processes in complex systems.
assessment.attribution: The Evans-Cohen-Morriss/Evans-Searles line gave the first fluctuation theorem, Jarzynski the nonequilibrium work relation, and Seifert the systematic trajectory-level stochastic thermodynamics. Crooks has a strong claim for the work-ratio relation but at most three can be named; I pick the three whose contributions are broadest. Priority among these and other contributors (e.g. Gallavotti-Cohen, Kurchan, Lebowitz-Spohn, who are not credited here) is a genuine allocation difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Single-molecule pulling experiments (RNA/DNA hairpins, optical tweezers) and colloidal and electronic tests have confirmed the relations for two decades, and the framework is now textbook. Recognition would be timely, though the field is still extending into quantum thermodynamics.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse: Crooks, Gallavotti, Cohen, Kurchan and others have strong claims and a three-person limit excludes some.
Practical consequences are mainly conceptual and in biophysics tools rather than a single landmark experiment.
I rely on memory for detailed priority dates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and its experimental realisation, opened topological band theory as a major field with a clean, general conceptual principle and many material realisations. It is a clear, lasting and original discovery with wide influence on condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and the theory; Molenkamp's group observed quantum spin Hall edge transport in HgTe wells (with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal not credited here); Hasan's group observed 3D topological insulators. The list includes both a 2D experimental and a 3D experimental claim, so a fair three-way split is arguable. I pick theory pair plus the first quantised-edge experiment.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmations across HgTe, Bi-based 3D materials and ARPES, transport and theory are strong; the interpretation is stable. Timing is good given that the 2016 prize recognised topological phases of matter but not this specific discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with candidates B007 and B004, which are partly overlapping parts of the same topological compound story.
Omission of Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan from the supplied credit, or Hasan's exclusion from my three, may be contested.
Overlap with the 2016 prize could make some members see this as already partly recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Halperin-Nelson-Young theory of two-dimensional melting via two-step defect unbinding and a hexatic phase is a landmark of statistical physics, applying defect-mediated phase transition ideas that I regard as fundamental. It has shaped understanding of soft, colloidal and 2D matter.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson formulated the dislocation-unbinding theory and the hexatic phase; Young independently developed the corresponding theory of the melting transition and elastic constants. Credit is clean, and Kosterlitz-Thouless is already recognised, which supports a coherent configuration.
assessment.maturity: The theory is about fifty years old and was confirmed in colloidal and simulation experiments, though details of the transition order for specific systems remained debated for decades. It is mature, perhaps overdue.
uncertainties: Some systems show first-order melting, so the universal two-step scenario is not exact everywhere.
Overlap with the 2016 prize for Kosterlitz-Thouless and the question of whether it is regarded as a sequel.
I am relying on memory for the history of the experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity created the field of moire quantum matter. It is original, with a simple theoretical principle and a very rich phenomenology.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group discovered correlated insulating states and superconductivity. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing, though others (e.g. Cao and Kim) have claims on the experimental side.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the main phases, but the origin of the superconductivity is not settled and the field is still moving fast. Recognition is arguably slightly early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity remains unresolved.
Experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero (first authors, Dean, Young, Kim groups) is contested.
Possibly premature relative to more mature candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have transformed time metrology, with implications for tests of fundamental physics. The achievement is outstanding experimentally and has wide impact, although it is a technical rather than a conceptual breakthrough.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated the strontium lattice clock; Ye's group brought it to the highest precision. The two-person configuration is clean, though Ye also appears in other candidates and Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent clocks agree and the field is mature; redefinition of the second is under discussion. Timely.
uncertainties: Limited conceptual novelty relative to the 2005 prize for frequency combs.
Other contributors (Lemonde, Hollberg, Ludlow, Schmidt) exist but are outside the supplied credit.
I have not verified current accuracy records.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed trapped-ion quantum gates and developed the theory of quantum simulation with cold atoms, founding experimental quantum information processing in atomic systems. The ideas are original and have been widely realised.
assessment.attribution: The two names are an established pair; the trapped-ion gate proposal is their joint work, while the experimental realisation (Wineland, Blatt and others) is not credited here, and Wineland already received the 2012 prize.
assessment.maturity: The proposals have been implemented across many platforms and are mature. Recognition is timely, although the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits and the 2012 prize on single-quantum-system control make some overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with other quantum-information candidates.
The theoretical-only credit may be considered less compelling than an experimental discovery.
I cannot verify the relative contribution of other theorists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation solves the horizon and flatness problems and gives a quantum origin for primordial fluctuations, with predictions confirmed in CMB spectra. It is among the most influential ideas in modern cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed inflation, Linde the new and chaotic inflation, and Mukhanov the quantum fluctuation calculation; Starobinsky, Chibisov and Steinhardt-Albrecht also have strong claims. Allocation is highly contested and a three-person division is arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: The CMB data support generic predictions such as near scale invariance, but no direct evidence, such as primordial gravitational waves, has been found, and alternatives exist. Recognition is arguably premature.
uncertainties: No direct detection of primordial B-modes.
Severe credit disputes (Starobinsky, Sato, Steinhardt, Albrecht).
This sits outside my own expertise, so I defer to colleagues on the cosmological evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gives a controlled non-perturbative treatment of strongly correlated electrons, based on the infinite-dimension limit, and underlies modern computational approaches to correlated materials. It is a conceptually elegant statistical-physics method.
assessment.attribution: Metzner-Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, Georges-Kotliar the mapping to an impurity problem, and Müller-Hartmann and Rozenberg also contributed; the credited trio is a plausible but not unique selection.
assessment.maturity: DMFT is firmly established and widely used, yet its status is that of a method rather than a discovery with a single decisive confirmation; its approximation breaks down in low dimensions.
uncertainties: Method-versus-discovery question for a physics prize.
Omitted contributors such as Metzner, Müller-Hartmann and Rozenberg.
Quality of predictions in real materials varies.
